newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker RGI have cash for NOK 7 bln buyout.
newsitem.headline: Aker RGI have cash for NOK 7 bln buyout.

text.p: Norwegian industrial holding company Aker RGI ASA could lay out up to seven billion crowns to expand its activities through an acquisition, the company said at an analysts presentation on Tuesday.
With a 30 percent debt gearing, Aker RGI is able to spend seven billion crowns to buy up a company, according to the group's financial analysis.
If it wanted to take a controlling stake in a concern, this would mean the acquisition target could have a value of up to 14 billion crowns.

This gives Aker RGI the power to buy most companies listed on the Oslo bourse, with the exception of heavyweight blue chips Norsk Hydro ASA, Orkla ASA, Kvaerner ASA, Saga Petroleum ASA, Den norske Bank ASA, Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA and Transocean ASA.
Speaking at a presentation of the group's annual results for 1996, CEO Bjoern Runne Gjelsten said Aker RGI was looking at many alternatives to expand and develop activities.
"We do not have any concrete plans for an acquisition, but we are working on many alternatives," Gjelsten said.
He declined to comment on any timeframe for plans, but said there could be one or more purchases.
"It could happen in a short time, or it might happen at the end of 1997," he said.
He said 20 to 30 percent would be a good debt gearing for Aker RGI, which, according to the company's analysis, would free up cash of around seven billion crowns.
